clue.text: Senior common room babel subsides — for grub

parts.note: SCR is the standard abbreviation for a university senior common room

indicators.note: a din that subsides collapses into a heap, so the word 'babel' falls into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder, five letters

explanation.surface: The dons' noisy common-room chatter dies down as dinner arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grub' looks like a noun for food but is the verb: to scrabble is to grub about, scratching with the hands. The answer is also the board game, in keeping with the puzzle's games theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean scratching or digging around with the hands in search of something.

clue.text: After spades lead card game gets serious

indicators.note: the card game is placed after the suit abbreviation in the answer
the suit leads, so it stands at the very front of the answer

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for the suit of spades
ombre is an old three-handed card game of Spanish origin

explanation.surface: A card player leads a spade and the game turns grim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' belongs to the surface only, borrowed from card play; OMBRE, popular in the 17th and 18th centuries, is a word worth knowing for crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Sombre describes a grave, gloomy mood, a close synonym of serious in tone.

clue.text: Republican line about rising generation of kings and queens

indicators.note: the party letter and the line letter go around the reversed generation word

parts.note: R is the usual abbreviation for Republican

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read from bottom to top, so the word for generation runs backwards

parts.note: an age is a generation or era
L is the standard abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A party member's view of how a new royal generation is coming up.
explanation.walkthrough: The two single letters R and L form the outside, with the reversed AGE sitting between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Regal is the adjective for anything belonging or fitting to monarchs, so kings and queens as a class.

clue.text: Lord Chancellor historically has limited metric weight and length covering amateur game

indicators.note: the statesman's surname has the other pieces confined within its bounds
the weight and length units cover the amateur by sitting either side of it

parts.note: Francis Bacon was Lord Chancellor under James I
kg, the kilogram, is the metric unit of weight
am is the usual abbreviation for amateur
m, the metre, is a unit of length

explanation.surface: A historic Lord Chancellor restricted to metric units while an amateur plays.
explanation.walkthrough: Francis Bacon, philosopher and Lord Chancellor to James I, is the setter's favourite 'historical' Lord Chancellor; the metric units are the SI abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Backgammon is a board game for two players moving counters by dice throws.

clue.text: Seven veils seductress

indicators.note: to veil is to conceal, so the first word keeps the answer covered inside it

parts.note: the middle three letters of this word

explanation.surface: Salome's Dance of the Seven Veils, the classic seductress's routine.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to Salome, but the seven veils are an instruction: 'Seven' veils the answer inside itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Eve tempted Adam with the forbidden fruit, making her the first temptress in Genesis.

clue.text: Hunted, caught and restrained

indicators.note: to catch what someone says is to hear it, so the word is taken by ear

parts.note: hunted means pursued, and the word for pursued is pronounced exactly like the answer

explanation.surface: A fugitive hunted down, captured and put in restraints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught' looks like part of the chase story, but here it means heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste means modest and self-controlled, holding back from indulgence, so restrained in conduct.

clue.text: Take in hostilities only Asterix ends

parts.note: HO, hostilities only, was a wartime enlistment for the duration of a conflict

indicators.note: only the extremities of the comic hero's name are wanted

parts.note: the first and last letters of the Gaulish hero's name

explanation.surface: Asterix the Gaul, fighting Romans, knows only war until the story ends.
explanation.walkthrough: HO is a wartime service abbreviation that crossword setters still use.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone in is to deceive them, and a hoax is exactly such a deception or trick.

clue.text: Yankees refined element identified by two nines and two ones

indicators.note: refining reworks raw material into a new form, so the team name is reworked into new order

parts.note: anagram fodder, seven letters
Es is the symbol for einsteinium, atomic number 99

explanation.surface: A chemistry puzzle: which refined element carries a pair of nines and a pair of ones?
explanation.walkthrough: Two nines is atomic number 99, einsteinium; its symbol joins the letters of YANKEES before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Snake eyes is the gamblers' name for a roll of two dice both showing a single spot.

clue.text: Players — i.e. the outfit selected for the match

definitions.meaning: a group of musicians or actors performing together

definitions.text: the outfit selected for the match
definitions.meaning: a set of clothes chosen so that every item matches

explanation.surface: A team sheet: the players picked for the big match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outfit' and 'match' pull toward a sports team, but the second sense is fashion: clothes chosen to match each other.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a troupe of performers and a coordinated set of garments worn together.

clue.text: Hogwarts subject Channel Islands school rejected

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the two pieces are turned round

parts.note: CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands
a gam is a school of whales

explanation.surface: A Channel Islands school turns down the Hogwarts curriculum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' is not a place of learning but a group of whales, a gam.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogwarts is the wizarding academy in the Harry Potter books, where pupils study spells and sorcery.

clue.text: Basque leader and separatists admit resistance and murder over breaches of trust

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of Basque

indicators.note: the separatist group lets the resistance letter in

parts.note: ETA was the Basque separatist group
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

indicators.note: in an across clue, 'over' means turned back, so the word for murder is read backwards

parts.note: to slay is to murder

explanation.surface: A news report on Basque separatists, resistance and killings.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is political news, and ETA fits it perfectly, which hides that it is only a three-letter building block.
explanation.definitionFit: A betrayal is the act of breaking someone's confidence or faith, so each one is a violation of loyalty.

clue.text: Pet hates? Guess one included ' 'ubby's a noisy sleeper'

parts.note: a bet is a guess at an outcome

indicators.note: the numeral for one is included inside the quoted phrase about the sleeper

parts.note: hubby is a noisy sleeper, i.e. he snores; dropping the H as the clue does gives 'E SNORES
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A wife listing pet hates: chiefly, her husband's snoring.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H of 'ubby' tells you to drop the H of 'he' too, giving 'E SNORES; I goes in after ESNO.
explanation.definitionFit: Bêtes noires, French for black beasts, are the things or people one particularly detests.

clue.text: Were the slow cycles bikes?

indicators.note: to cycle is to go round, so the first three words are rotated into a new arrangement

parts.note: anagram fodder, eleven letters

explanation.surface: A question about whether those sluggish old cycles were really bikes.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: 'cycles' shuffles the fodder, and the question as a whole describes bicycles.
explanation.definitionFit: Bicycles and motorbikes each run on a pair of wheels, which is exactly what the compound names.

clue.text: Entire goal difference may determine it

definitions.text: Entire goal difference may determine it

indicators.note: a difference is a change, so the two words take a changed order

parts.note: anagram fodder, ten letters

explanation.surface: A football table where goal difference settles who goes down.
explanation.walkthrough: Goal difference is the football tie-breaker for teams level on points, and at the foot of the league it decides who drops a division.
explanation.definitionFit: Relegation is demotion of a sports club to a lower league, often settled on tie-breakers at season's end.

clue.text: Match requiring two moves to mate

indicators.note: shifting two letters of the final word rearranges it into the answer

parts.note: anagram fodder, four letters

explanation.surface: A chess game where checkmate comes in two moves.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess surface hides a letter game: move the M to the end and the T to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To team things is to pair them so they go together, one sense of the verb match.

clue.text: Maybe Alex, Eric and Ernie's day out?

definitions.meaning: Alex is a long-running cartoon about a City banker in the Daily Telegraph
Morecambe and Wise were comedians, so their outing is the comics' outing

explanation.surface: A trip out for three friends called Alex, Eric and Ernie.
explanation.walkthrough: Eric Morecambe and Ernie Wise were a much-loved British comedy double act; split the answer as COMICS TRIP for the second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Alex is an example of a cartoon series told in panels, and comedians' excursion re-spaces into the same letters.

clue.text: Methods used in training sessions for Olympics? They'll keep serving men

parts.note: the Olympics are the Olympic Games

indicators.note: the pronoun keeps the serving men inside it, holding them within

parts.note: the pronoun, stripped of its 'will'
OR is other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Coaches preparing athletes for the Olympics and the kit-carrying staff behind them.
explanation.walkthrough: Games theory here is the educational approach of teaching sport through playing games, not the economists' game theory; 'serving men' are soldiers in the ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: It names a coaching approach, a set of teaching principles applied during practice and drills.

clue.text: Grace's kit should be reviewed as guide to selectors

indicators.note: reviewing implies going over again, so the letters are gone over into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder, nine letters

explanation.surface: W.G. Grace's cricket kit being inspected by the team selectors.
explanation.walkthrough: W.G. Grace was the great Victorian cricketer, and selectors pick cricket teams; here the selectors are a car's gears.
explanation.definitionFit: The lever in a manual car guides the gearbox mechanism that selects which gear is engaged.

clue.text: Perhaps Jacob's socially acceptable bow you rehearsed again and again

indicators.note: re-heard means heard again, and the repetition applies to each of the three items in turn

parts.note: U means upper-class and socially acceptable
longbows were made of yew wood
the word itself, spoken

explanation.surface: A shepherd practising courtly bows to his sheep over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: Four words sound alike: U, yew, you and the answer; the clue gives three and asks for the fourth. U and non-U were Nancy Mitford's labels for upper-class and non-upper-class usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jacob is a breed of spotted, often many-horned sheep, so a female one is an example.

clue.text: Once 45 is divided by 10 and 50 and 100 by 1, information technology makes it unambiguous

indicators.note: one numeral stands beside the other two, placed next to them in sequence
splitting the record into two parts leaves room for the Roman ten between them

parts.note: an EP, extended play, was a record played at 45 rpm
X is the Roman numeral ten
L is the Roman numeral fifty
I is the Roman numeral one
C is the Roman numeral a hundred
IT is the standard abbreviation for information technology

explanation.surface: An arithmetic exercise that computing will finally make clear.
explanation.walkthrough: The sums are a false trail: 45 is a record speed, and the other numbers are Roman numerals placed between and beside letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Explicit means stated clearly and in full, leaving no room for doubt or multiple readings.

clue.text: Cross in eastern Spain 'river of no return'? On the contrary

definitions.text: 'river of no return'? On the contrary

indicators.note: the cross sits inside the pair of one-letter abbreviations

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for eastern
a cross is the letter X
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A river in eastern Spain, famed like the film as a river of no return.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition flips the film title River of No Return: this river reads the same both ways, so it does return. The Exe flows through Devon to Exeter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Exe is an English river whose name reads identically forwards and backwards, so it comes back.

clue.text: Penitent's defence of Christianity

parts.note: someone penitent is sorry for what they did
the possessive ending supplies its letter

explanation.surface: A sinner's plea in their own defence before the church.
explanation.walkthrough: An apology in the old sense is a formal defence, not a statement of regret, which is why the surface works.
explanation.definitionFit: Apologetics is the branch of theology that argues reasoned justification for religious doctrine.

clue.text: A yell's evoked when taws is brought out

definitions.note: describes the answer as what appears when the game of taws is played

indicators.note: to evoke is to call forth, so the letters are called out in a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder, six letters

explanation.surface: A shout goes up when the tawse, the Scottish leather strap, comes out.
explanation.walkthrough: Taws is a game of marbles (and a taw a shooting marble), and alleys are marbles; the surface suggests the tawse, a strap once used for school punishment in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Alleys are choice playing marbles, originally of alabaster, which are brought out whenever a marbles game is played.

clue.text: Scots love having entered second to come second

indicators.note: the abbreviation has gone into the Scots word, sitting inside it

parts.note: lo'e is the Scots form of love, as in Burns
s is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A Scot in love, entering a contest only to finish runner-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' appears twice: first as the letter S, then inside the definition, where finishing second means not winning.
explanation.definitionFit: In a two-way contest, finishing behind the winner means being beaten.

clue.text: Greek letter — in Greek — is re‑read before Latin war game

indicators.note: the shuffled group comes ahead of the Latin abbreviation
the letter name sits inside the nationality word before anything moves
reading again in a different way produces the letters in a changed order

parts.note: the word itself, as fodder
the word itself, as fodder
pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
L is the abbreviation for Latin

explanation.surface: A classics lesson: a Greek letter, read twice, set beside the Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: The Greek and Latin surface hides a German answer: Kriegspiel was a Prussian army training game, and also a chess variant played without seeing the opponent's pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The German word literally means war play, a tabletop simulation for training military officers.

clue.text: 1 and 1 can make I

indicators.note: the three words can be made into something else by rearranging them

parts.note: each 1 is the Roman numeral I, joined by 'and'

explanation.surface: A child's arithmetic: one plus one can make one.
explanation.walkthrough: The sum 1 and 1 suggests two, but the numbers are Roman I's, and the lone I is a letter in the radio alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: In the NATO phonetic alphabet used by radio operators, the code word for the ninth letter is this country.

clue.text: Bowl round wicket to get man

indicators.note: the vessel goes round the cricket abbreviation, enclosing it

parts.note: a pan is a bowl-shaped vessel
w is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wicket

explanation.surface: Cricket advice: bowl round the wicket to dismiss the batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowl round the wicket' is a genuine cricket instruction about which side of the stumps the bowler runs; here the bowl is a pan.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess pieces are called men, and the smallest of them is a pawn.

clue.text: Chest protectors militant Republicans will find d—- d, d—– d confining

indicators.note: the swearing words confine the militants by holding them inside

parts.note: printed with dashes, these are swear words, which are cusses
the IRA was the Irish Republican Army

explanation.surface: Soldiers in body armour, with militants swearing blind all round them.
explanation.walkthrough: The dashed words are 'damned, damned' printed politely; such oaths are cusses.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuirass is a piece of armour made of a breastplate and backplate, guarding the torso.

clue.text: Regard for 50% of partnerships scoring in bridge

indicators.note: half of each word is wanted, the second half in each case

parts.note: one partnership is headed THEY on a bridge score pad; its second half is kept
the other partnership is headed WE on the score pad; its second half is kept

explanation.surface: Due credit for the pairs who score well at a bridge club.
explanation.walkthrough: The two partnerships at a bridge table are recorded as WE and THEY on the score pad; keep the back half of each, THEY first.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard something is to look at it, and to eye it is to watch it closely.

clue.text: State Department game discards American crest

indicators.note: the game throws away the nationality abbreviation, leaving what remains

parts.note: RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island
d is the abbreviation for department
the word itself, before the cut
Am is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: The US State Department dropping an American emblem from a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State Department' is the US foreign ministry in the surface, but splits into two abbreviations; GAME without AM leaves GE.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge is the long narrow top of a hill or mountain range, its summit line.

clue.text: Changing course college fails to make attractive

indicators.note: the college abbreviation fails to appear, so it is dropped

parts.note: a sailing boat changes course by tacking
c is the abbreviation for college

explanation.surface: A student switching courses when the college lets them down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changing course' is academic in the surface but nautical in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking as an adjective means charming or captivating, an old-fashioned word for appealing.

clue.text: Makes opponents lead to 20 goals cramping sport

indicators.note: to cramp is to squeeze in, so the goals squeeze the sport between them

parts.note: ends are aims or goals
sport and play are synonyms

explanation.surface: A football team scores twenty goals despite being cramped.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 points to 20 across, LOSE: in bridge an endplay throws an opponent on lead so that any card they play costs their side a trick.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, an endplay is a late-hand manoeuvre forcing defenders into a lead that sacrifices tricks.
